title: Cross-pod orientation flow and KT matrix
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working playbook for orienting new hires who will span multiple pods (cross-pod hires). Focus is on a 14-day micro-onboard that prioritizes fast context, measurable knowledge-transfer (KT) handoffs, and lightweight interview/confirmation checkpoints so pod partners and hiring managers have shared signals.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: hiring manager + buddy + pod leads + people-ops onboarding coordinator.
- Scope: ICs (SWE, SRE, ML infra) and contractors transitioning toward perm roles or cross-functional contributors.
- Not a replacement for full 90-day plan — this is the 0–14 rapid assimilation slice.

Principles (quick):
- 2-week timebox with daily objectives, short meetings only when high-value.
- Work-in-public: KT docs live in the pod repo/drive and labeled "KT-ready".
- Measurable: every KT topic has a owner, artifacts, and a confirmation check.
- Lightweight evidence: use 30-min demo sessions and a 10-point check rubric to confirm understanding.

Top-level flow (14 days, high level):
- Day 0 (pre-join): account provisioning checklist + welcome note from pod.
- Days 1–3: orientation + infra tour + critical runbook walk-throughs.
- Days 4–7: paired shadow sessions and small sandbox tasks.
- Days 8–11: KT deliverable: doc + short demo + acceptance by owner.
- Days 12–14: handoff sign-off, follow-up backlog, and 14-day retro with hiring manager.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Hiring manager: final acceptance, sets 14-day priorities, attends Day 14 retro.
- Buddy (peer): daily check-ins, coordinates pairing, acts as first-line reviewer of KT artifacts.
- Pod owner/SME: owns each KT topic, runs demos, accepts deliverables.
- People Ops: sends templates, schedules Day 0/14, records artifacts.

Pre-join checklist (Day 0, quick):
- Provision: GitHub, Slack, Okta groups, cloud project access. Responsible: IT (cc: buddy).
- Access to key docs: pod README, runbooks, incident playbooks, on-call rota.
- Small intro doc from hiring manager: 3 priority goals for first 30 days (one-liner each).

Day-by-day microplan (concise):
- Day 1 (welcome): 30m intro with hiring manager + 30m buddy sync. Set 3 priorities, environment smoke test.
- Day 2 (infra tour): 60m infra/runbook deep-dive led by SRE SME. Attempt a read-only run of the main deployment pipeline.
- Day 3 (observability): 45m dashboard and alerting review; identify 1 alert to investigate as sandbox task.
- Day 4 (pair1): Pair on a small bugfix or config change (buddy). 1-hour pairing session.
- Day 5 (shadow-oncall): Shadow oncall rotation and look at recent incident postmortems.
- Day 6 (pair2): Pair with a different pod SME on cache/kv layer or model serving path.
- Day 7 (mini-deliverable): Submit a short doc: "how I would change X if I had 30% more time" (2–3 bullets). Pod feedback due Day 9.
- Days 8–9 (KT docs): Prepare KT deliverable docs for 2 topics. Schedule 30m demo slots with owners.
- Day 10 (demo1): Demo topic A + acceptance checklist.
- Day 11 (demo2): Demo topic B + acceptance checklist.
- Day 12 (cleanup): Address feedback, tidy docs, mark artifacts KT-ready.
- Day 13 (pre-signoff): Buddy run-through, final checklist.
- Day 14 (retro & signoff): 30m retro with hiring manager, record decisions, map next-stage 30/60 actions.

KT Matrix (template to fill — keep short):
Columns: Topic | Owner | Artifact (doc/link) | Demo date | Acceptance (Y/N) | Evidence notes
Example row (text):
- Topic: Deploy pipeline quickstart | Owner: Marco Rivera | Artifact: repo/ops/deploy-kt.md | Demo date: 2025-07-09 | Acceptance: Y | Evidence notes: completed dry run + small config PR merged

Acceptance rubric (10-point quick checklist — use for each demo):
- Can describe purpose of system in 2–3 sentences (1)
- Walk through the main incident flow (1)
- Run a read-only smoke check in the environment (1)
- Identify two common failure modes (1)
- Locate the core runbook and explain where to escalate (1)
- Make a trivial config change + open PR (1)
- Explain monitoring signals (1)
- Reproduce a non-blocking alert locally or in sandbox (1)
- Point to 1 improvement idea and rationale (1)
- Show artifact is correctly labeled and stored (1)

Interview/confirmation checkpoint (used when converting contractor->perm or for cross-pod signoffs):
- 20-min synchronous checkpoint with hiring manager + 1 SME. Use the acceptance rubric, record yes/no for each line. Always keep transcript/notes in the KT doc.
- If any acceptance line is No, list remediation tasks and schedule a follow-up checkpoint within 7 days.

Artifact labeling convention (must):
- Title prefix: "KT - <topic> - <name/owner>"
- Metadata header (first lines): owner, date, pod, demo link.
- Tag in Drive: people-ops/onboard/KT-ready

Evidence storage locations (quick):
- Primary: pod drive folder -> onboarding/KT/
- Backup: repo/docs/kt/
- Meeting recordings: people-ops/onboard/recordings/ (link to be added)

Example small-sandbox tasks (15–60m):
- Run the deploy pipeline in dry-run and capture output.
- Write a tiny automated test for a flaky alert.
- Update a doc section and open PR.

Templates to paste (short):
- 3-priority goals email (hire mgr -> new hire): Hi <name>, first 3 things I want you to focus on: 1) Learn X, 2) Observe Y, 3) Ship small Z. Short expectations + who to ping if blocked.
- Demo invite subject: "KT demo: <topic> — 30m — <owner>". Agenda: 5m context, 15m demo, 5m Q, 5m acceptance check.

Common pitfalls & guardrails (notes to self):
- Don’t overload demos — 2 topics only in first 2 weeks.
- Avoid admin-heavy tasks — focus on visible changes and confidence-building.
- Ensure access is resolved before demos — schedule a backup demo slot if access fails.

Open questions / To decide:
- Do we require a minimal number of KT topics for contractors being converted? (proposed: 2)
- Can we centralize storage labeling with an automated tag (people-ops team to follow up with infra)?

Logistics and Slack snippets (copyable):
- Buddy ping message: "Welcome <name> — I’m your buddy. Today: 1) quick environment check, 2) join infra tour at 11am. Ping me in #pod-ops if stuck."
- Demo reminder message (24h before): "Reminder: KT demo <topic> with <owner> tomorrow at <time>. Please post the doc link in thread."

14-day retro template (quick):
- Wins (2–3 bullets)
- Blockers (2–3 bullets)
- What to carry into 30-day plan (3 prioritized items)
- Signoff: hiring manager confirms acceptance (Y/N) and next steps

Appendix: quick checklist that buddy uses every day (daily):
- Morning: 15m sync + surface blockers.
- End of day: quick note in KT doc — what was done, share any PR links.
- If demo scheduled: confirm access + test recording function 30m early.

Notes to people-ops (admin):
- We should create a Drive label "KT-ready" and grant pod leads ability to set it.
- Consider a 1-page dashboard that lists active KT topics and acceptance status (could be a sheet).

——
Working draft — iterative. Use this as a fill-in template for cross-pod hires. Feedback welcome — please leave comments inline or ping me (Aisha) on Slack.
